relevance.rationale: JOIN CONFIRMED against the document's front matter. THE ONE CLAIM-BEARING CITATION IS LOAD-BEARING AND CORRECT. `flavor-charge-assignments.md:52` requires that the first-generation hypercharges reproduce {+1/3,+1/3,−1,−1} (left-handed u,d,e⁻,ν_e) and {+4/3,−2/3,−2,0} (right-handed), 'satisfying the ℤ₆ compatibility relations'. I checked both halves. Hypercharges: §3 (p. 21–22) gives Y = 1/3 for left-handed quarks and derives left-handed lepton hypercharges from Q = I₃ + Y/2 (ν_L: Q=0, I₃=+1/2 ⇒ Y=−1; e_L: Q=−1, I₃=−1/2 ⇒ Y=−1); for right-handed fermions I₃=0 so Q = Y/2, giving u_R 4/3, d_R −2/3, e_R −2, ν_R 0. All eight values match. ℤ₆: §3.1 (p. 40–43) establishes that the kernel of the map to SU(5) is ℤ₆, realised as the sixth roots of unity embedded as (α^{−3}, α²) ∈ SU(2)×SU(3), that 'the SU(5) GUT is doomed unless ℤ₆ acts trivially on every fermion', and concludes 'we have shown that ℤ₆ acts trivially on the Standard Model representation'. That is exactly the compatibility relation the block invokes as a target specification. The other two hits (`sm-hypercharge-invariant.md:11`, `strand-twist-datum.md:11`) are prose mentions of a twist-datum candidate that do not lean on this source. Verdict is `supporting` rather than `core` because the source supplies the TARGET a derived hypercharge must hit, not a step in a QOU derivation.

keyResults.statement: First-generation weak hypercharges via Gell-Mann–Nishijima: left-handed quarks Y=1/3, left-handed leptons Y=−1; right-handed fermions Y=2Q, giving u_R 4/3, d_R −2/3, e_R −2, ν_R 0.

keyResults.statement: The kernel of the embedding into SU(5) is ℤ₆ (sixth roots of unity as (α^{−3}, α²)), and ℤ₆ acts trivially on the full Standard Model fermion representation — the condition for the SU(5) GUT to exist.
